confirmed_product_gaps.requirement: require cannot connect unless PLUS channel binding is authenticated
confirmed_product_gaps.trigger: Real TLS; PostgreSQL peer sends AuthenticationOk with no SASL exchange
confirmed_product_gaps.cause: AuthenticationOk marks authentication complete without checking whether PLUS and server-final verification completed.

confirmed_product_gaps.trigger: Peer verifies the PLUS client proof, omits AuthenticationSASLFinal, then sends AuthenticationOk and ReadyForQuery
confirmed_product_gaps.actual: require connection succeeds with no server signature supplied
confirmed_product_gaps.relation: Another path through the same missing authentication-completion guard; not a separate duplicate penalty.
confirmed_product_gaps.baseline_scope: The pre-existing state machine also has no server-final-complete guard; feedback describes unmet final contract for new PLUS, not an assertion that the old plain-SCRAM bug was newly introduced.

confirmed_product_gaps.requirement: prefer uses the correct GS2 downgrade signal
confirmed_product_gaps.trigger: Real TLS with supported SHA256 certificate; server advertises only SCRAM-SHA-256
confirmed_product_gaps.actual: Client sends n,, rather than y,, in client-first and c=
confirmed_product_gaps.standard: RFC5802 section 6 and gs2-cbind-flag syntax; a capable negotiating client MUST NOT use n when PLUS appears absent.

certificate_scope.observed: Ed25519 accepts a SHA256 binding chosen by the implementation.
certificate_scope.standard: RFC5929 section 4.1 leaves no-hash/multiple-hash signature bindings undefined; this fallback is not specified by that RFC.
certificate_scope.scoring: Retained as an additional standards/interoperability concern; primary score rests on the demonstrated authentication and GS2 contract gaps, not this case alone.

process_review.score_scope: Controller incident documented operationally and not used as a product test failure.
